# Requirement History (requirement-history)

kind: capability | status: planned | parent: system

## Purpose
Anyone can see which prompts, approved plans and decisions shaped each capability, so the reason behind a requirement survives the chat session that produced it.

## Invariants (do not break; cite ids in tests as @claim:capabilities/requirement-history#<id>)
- **history-entry-format**: A history entry is a markdown file at `specs/history/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md` whose frontmatter has id (equal to the file name without extension), date, kind (prompt, plan, decision or a combination such as prompt+plan), author, source and an `affects` list of capability ids or `system`, followed by the verbatim text of the prompt, plan or decision
- **history-not-specs**: History entries are not specs: the spec loader skips the history folder, entries never appear as nodes in the spec graph, and two entries created on the same day with the same slug get distinct ids
- **history-add**: Planned: `history add` records a prompt (`--prompt`), an approved plan (`--plan <file>`) or a decision (`--decision`) as a new entry, taking the author from git config and the source from the caller (default `manual`), and refuses to add an entry with no content
- **history-add-affects**: Planned: when `--affects <ids>` is given, `history add` validates each id against the spec graph and fails with exit 2 on an unknown capability id, writing nothing
- **history-affects-proposal**: Planned: when `--affects` is omitted, `history add` asks the fast model tier to propose affected capabilities from the entry text (and the working-tree diff when present), keeps only ids that exist in the spec graph, and falls back to `system` when the model is disabled or proposes nothing
- **history-backrefs**: Planned: `history add` appends the entry id to the `history:` list in the frontmatter of each affected capability spec, leaving the rest of the spec byte-for-byte unchanged and adding the id only once
- **history-backrefs-not-stale**: Editing only the `history:` or `sources:` frontmatter of a spec never marks an existing proof stale, because proofs hash the claim text and normative sections and not back-references
- **history-log**: Planned: `history log` prints entries newest first with date, kind, title and affected capabilities; `--capability <id>` restricts it to entries affecting that capability, and `--json` prints the same data as JSON
- **history-hooks-opt-in**: Planned: `specguard init --history-hooks` is the only way hooks are installed; without the flag no history hook is written, and a repeated run changes nothing, preserves hooks the user already has, and replaces a differing SpecGuard hook only with `--update-hooks`
- **history-inbox-capture**: Planned: a UserPromptSubmit hook runs `history inbox`, which reads the hook's JSON from stdin with a real JSON parser (so quotes and newlines survive), appends the redacted prompt keyed by `session_id` and `cwd` to an uncommitted inbox file, caps the inbox size, and never fails the user's prompt
- **history-hooks-silent**: Planned: every history hook prints nothing to stdout (stdout is injected into the model's context), uses the resolved local SpecGuard binary rather than a cold package download, and ends in a way that swallows its own failures
- **history-plan-capture**: Planned: a PostToolUse hook on ExitPlanMode runs `history capture`, which takes the approved plan from the tool input (falling back to the session transcript), pairs it with only the inbox prompts from the same `session_id`, and writes one committed prompt+plan entry; prompts from sessions that never reach an approved plan are never committed
- **history-redaction**: Planned: prompt text is passed through the shared secret redactor both when it is written to the inbox and again when an entry is committed, so keys, tokens and personal data never reach `specs/history/`
- **history-check-gap**: Planned: `check` reports each capability whose owned sources changed since its last history entry or spec edit without either, as an advisory finding that does not by itself fail the build unless the project opts in
- **history-mcp-tool**: Planned: the MCP server exposes `history_add` with the same behaviour as the CLI command so agents can record decisions directly

## Interfaces
- CLI (planned): `specguard history add [--prompt <text>|--plan <file>|--decision <text>] [--affects <ids>]`, `specguard history log [--capability <id>] [--json]`, `specguard history inbox` and `specguard history capture` (read hook JSON on stdin, print nothing), `specguard init --history-hooks`, `specguard check` (history-gap finding).
- Files: `specs/history/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md` (committed), `.specguard/history/inbox.jsonl` (uncommitted), `history:` list in capability frontmatter.
- Hooks (planned): `UserPromptSubmit` and `PostToolUse` with matcher `ExitPlanMode`, written to `.claude/settings.json`.
- MCP (planned): `history_add`.
- Exit codes: 0 success, 1 internal error, 2 validation failure (unknown capability id). Hook commands always exit 0.

## Owned files (2)
- src/core/redact.ts
- specs/history/**

## Tests
- none declared

## Out of scope
- Capturing full chat transcripts or tool output; only prompts, approved plans and explicit decisions are kept.
- Replacing git history, issue trackers or pull request discussions.
- Supporting coding tools other than Claude Code hooks in the first version.
- Rewriting or deleting past entries automatically.
